steps.text: Baron Peter Lukas turns seventy-three this year.
He inherited his title from his uncle three years ago. Six months later, he moved to Karl Schmidt Street due to the expenses of maintaining the Lukas family spire.
He enjoys Karl Schmidt's music, but hates the street.
He finds the sunlight, the flowers, the youth's graffiti, and the jazz music coming from the nearby bar unbearable.
He orders his servant to close the curtains, turns on the gramophone, and the room is immediately filled with the sound of cello.
The Sankta was a truly talented musician, he thinks. So talented, he could almost forgive her for being Lateran.
He plays eleven instruments, ten of which he learned during the reign of the Witch King.
To send the best melodies into the Genesis Spire, talented young musicians were put into a room and made to compose day and night.
He loved the violinist, her delicate fingers, and the beauty mark on the edge of her palm.
Tears flowed down his face when he visited Victoria for the first time and heard music from his homeland on the stage of the Royal Theater. He kissed her for the first time.
That was his elegant, dignified Leithanien.
He misses it.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Trying to destroy houses and escape in the chaos?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: There is nowhere for you to hide before the Golden Melody.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Mmph—Argh!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You're the last.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Remove your mask and surrender to Leithanien, and you will be spared the pain of a burning soul.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: This pain is... insignificant.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Have you ever heard the Witch King's Reichsorchester play?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The black forests of Einwald, the lakes and ports of Fortsgard, the storms of Sturmland... anything you can imagine about Leithanien, you could feel in the melody.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The Witch King did not interpret or conduct. He simply walked amongst them.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: As one of his musicians, you had to follow the guidance of his sightline, and keep a tight pace with him. Fall out of line, and you were ripped apart by the magnificent melody.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Witch King's favorite punishment for those too weak to serve him.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: But I kept up.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: I became a part of that transcendent melody. Since then, I could no longer tolerate playing for the mediocre.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: What did you think you were? Interpreters of the great melody? Ideal-driven revolutionaries?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Nein.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: All I see are criminals hiding behind masks, killing the innocents of Leithanien and undermining her peace and order... Clowns, burying their faces in the embers of the Witch King.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Your life belongs to the Golden Melody now.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: But I suppose you were already dead, from the moment you gave up your free will and become the Witch King's vassal.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Agh... hah... haha!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: And what about you then? Aren't you wearing a mask yourself?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The Arts you use: the Golden Melody, the light of Leithanien, passed down through generations of Gesatzswächter, those who guard the Güldenesgesatz—

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Are you not also a servant of a melody written by a greater will?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Even the greatest individual will is nothing before Leithanien herself.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Then...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Is it Leithanien's Golden Melody that pronounces my death sentence, or you yourself?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Is this your escape plan? Did you think the will of the Gesatzswächter would waver before such cliches?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Preposterous.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Why... would I need an escape plan?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: I was... chosen to find you.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The Concertmaster wants to know.... When the events of twenty-three years ago echoed in your ears just now...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Did you see Ernst von Hochberg, for whom help would never arrive in time...?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Or his brother Werner, who died in sorrow as the Kurfürst he never wanted to be?
The Witch King cultist's body turns to dust under the power of dual Originium Arts.
Only her last words remain with the ashes.

a.text: You cannot avoid a choice forever.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: On that day, twenty-three years ago, Father didn't wait for Mother.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They missed each other.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Lucinda went to the spice market before coming to the studio that morning. She wanted to try a different incense, see if it would lift her spirits.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: She did not know that she was already with child.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mother went to Sturmland in the end.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: She loved you, and she loved Werner. She could not have raised you on her own if she'd stayed in Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: She knew that Werner had already gotten married, but she had no other choice.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Father had a choice.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ten minutes. If Werner had waited another ten minutes, he'd have met Lucinda and known that she was willing to face it all and fight by his side.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He... regretted those ten minutes for the rest of his life.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He never told me, but I knew.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A marigold and the moon... it was never meant to be. It was a dream that, upon waking, they knew to be beyond reach, words spoken only to comfort.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Don't you blame your father?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I can't.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: We're too alike.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You told me that he aspired to be a poet.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But he never once recited a poem in front of me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It was only after I returned to Leithanien that I realized... When someone no longer has the strength to face reality, the illusions that once brought hope now bring only pain.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You've been busy since your father's passing, shuttling from Sturmland to Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: All I want to say is... it's alright to express your sorrow.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I just want to rest for a while.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Just for a little while.
Cora says no more. She closes the curtains before she leaves.
The darkness wraps around Viviana like a familiar blanket. Cora knows her well, knows what brings her comfort.
She gazes upon the paintings in the room, now covered in shadow, and the golden times depicted within gaze back at her.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Fortunately, the Arts in that music didn't cause Viviana any real damage.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But they brought back memories of Werner, as they did for us. And it must be even more painful for her.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You're injured.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I am?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Oh... this wasn't from the battle. I might have bumped myself when I went downstairs chasing after Viviana.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Why not try the therapeutic machine I brought back from Columbia?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I didn't lose my eyesight yesterday, Brandt. I've managed on my own for the past twenty-some years.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You, though... something's off with your voice. Were these enemies that tough?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: What an absurd notion.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: That's more like you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I wish you'd take off your helmet and catch your breath once in a while, though. Even the finest instrument succumbs to wear and tear when used nonstop.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I don't deserve to rest.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Gendarmerie is on their way. They'll take it from here.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You should leave before they arrive.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Now? But we're so close to the truth.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Leithanien has not fallen so far as to need to entrust her future to a blind instrument tuner and a retired competition knight.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The cultists are looking for the Witch King's legacy. Frieda and Loris were witnesses to that night. Werner... House Hochberg was part of the coup as well.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: If they're killing witnesses to complete some sort of ritual, they'll be looking for their next target.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Which is why you need to listen to me and stop your investigation.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: What about you, Brandt? You were there on the day of the coup too...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I am a guardian of Leithanien's will. A few Witch King worshippers won't get me.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Besides, they laid an ambush for you here. You're the ones they're targeting.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But how did they know we were coming? Could Viviana really be right, and Frieda's paintings hold an important clue?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I believe so.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Reiner, please allow me to continue the investigation. I want to know what Frau Seemann left behind.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You're... holding the draft to her final work.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: 'Regret.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The strongest emotion and desire that the painter had ever felt in her life.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She spent her last days painting it over and over again.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Through the strokes of her brush, she wanted to see the divine in her heart.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You're saying those haphazard strokes were intentional?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja. It looks messy because she painted on the same sheet over and over again.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The scene of the Witch King's death is still in the draft.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Put the painting on the ground, Viviana.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Brandt, try to 'play' it.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Tell me when to stop.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's vibrating, like a musical instrument.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: There are minute differences in each layer of paint.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can't see, but my Arts allow me to 'hear' the frequency of each layer.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Almost there... just remove the layer of paint above, and we'll find...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The very first version.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Do you see it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's blurry, but I can tell that it's the interior of a spire. It's... imposing.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Witch King's Spire. I imagine that even Frieda could only paint a small part of it.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Can you identify the figures in the painting?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: There is no Witch King. The throne is empty. The battle seems to be over.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The painter herself, Frieda Seemann, is behind the curtain.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: There is a Liberi soldier charging in from the hallway... Loris Bordin?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And... um...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Who is this Caprinae holding an Arts unit and cleaning up?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Gerhard Hoffmann.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: One of the most talented casters in all of Einwald, formerly in service to House Urtica.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: He became a teacher after the Witch King's death.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: We were late.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: These lunatics don't care how many innocents they kill.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: *cough*... *cough*.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're injured. I can treat your wounds.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Danke.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Where is Baron Lukas? Is he upstairs?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The Baron... didn't make it.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: He'd been talking about moving for a while. We wouldn't have gotten caught up in all this if we hadn't put the plans on hold just because of that Sankta cellist playing in the area!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What did their performance sound like?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Do you want to hear it? The Baron had me record it. I wonder if the gramophone's still alright...

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Huh, you actually found a clue.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin found it.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Is it Arturia?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I may not be able to recognize a live performance or not, but I would never mistake her playing.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Aren't we in trouble then?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No need to fear. There are no Arts in the recording, and she isn't nearby. Someone broadcasted her performance on this street a few minutes ago.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: And her Arts worked over such a large area?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She must have accomplices. It would only be possible through a combination of Leithanian Arts and her own.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: You can tell all that just from listening to this?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This section here. It's not the sound of a cello. It's a pipe organ, and one of uncommon size.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: A huge pipe organ...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It's an unusual instrument. Where might you find one in Zwillingstürme?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...Ludwigs-Universität.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A school?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Ja. It used to be the spire of learning for House Urtica.
His head hurts.
He has not felt such pain since he escaped Vyseheim.
When was the last time it hurt so much that he wanted to scream, to vomit, to cry?
It was...
He could remember. He just didn't want to.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Say something.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Gloat, why don't you? You're on the cusp of victory, after I've kept you trapped in my head for so long.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When I die... I sure hope I get a proper death.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Unlike you, who's been dead long enough to crumble to dust, only to be pieced back together and brought back to life.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: What is he babbling about?

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: You haven't started the ritual yet, have you?
Not yet, Professor.
He looks like he's in pain. Can he really take it?

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: He's from Herkunftshorn's bloodline. If he can't take even this much, then Ewigegnade must have intentionally raised him to be useless.
He's suffered much for his age.
If he's unable to bear it, interrupting the performance of the Voice of Mundane could cause the Genesis Horn to go out of control and affect all of Ludwig.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: I'm here. The spire will hold.
But you swore an oath to Her Majesty that you would not reveal the true extent of your powers. She'd have to answer to the nobles if the students learned of your identity.
Ludwigs-Universität may be shut down, which would affect your relocation plans.
And Ermi will give you an earful when she gets back to Leithanien.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: ...Bah. Keeping this boy alive is harder than summoning the Genesis Horn.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Where is Lessing?
He's standing watch outside.
He said he'll ensure that no one can enter before the ritual is complete.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Pah, nothing more than keeping his mind from being torn to pieces. Where is the device I made for those nutjobs in Bolívar?
Are you alright?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hah...
It's okay. They've left the room.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're...

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: We met not too long ago.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Forest... Park...

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Ja. I wanted to warn you, but Lessing was there. I couldn't take you away with him watching.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Lessing...

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: He's not evil by nature, but he can be stubborn.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I used to be like him too. But all it takes to change is courage.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Can you move? Try to grab my hand.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: What are you doing, Gerhard?!

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I'm sorry, Professor.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I can't let you use Herkunftshorn's bloodline like this. He's a living, breathing soul, one with a bright future.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Spatial defense Arts— I taught you those!

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: You also taught me that even the most powerful Arts cannot erase regret.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I've caused a lot of harm with the Arts you taught me.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: But when I'm alone at night, I often ask myself: how many souls would have continued to shine brightly, had I not done what I did?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Would we be living in better times? Would the people around us have been better? Would we be better ourselves?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: That's why I gave up on being a spire caster and became a scholar.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: What are you babbling about, Gerhard?

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: You're making a big mistake. Step away from the boy—

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: ...A mistake?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Nein, Professor.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I'm saving his life. I'm not going to miss my chance this time. I'm fixing the biggest mistake that you and I... that we ever made.
